g.text: The only path a policy could leave the machine, and every point that refuses first
the bounded envelope goes in; the serializer
emits approved fields, never the raw record
disabled until budgeted; the attempt is reserved
and a failure does not refund it
https origin and path are pinned, so the caller
chooses neither; a second in-flight call is refused
read in 1 KiB chunks before JSON is parsed;
an oversized body is cut off, not truncated
The attempt is spent and its quota is not refunded, so a failure cannot quietly become a loop; and the error
carries a code, so provider text and response headers never reach the caller. The mock adapter sits behind the
same boundary, so the demo exercises these refusals instead of bypassing them, and a real provider would
inherit every check without a call site changing.
Constants read from backend/app/provider_safety.py on 2026-10-30: 16 KiB request, 4 KiB response, 20 s timeout, 17 attempts, $5.00.
